task_format: Gamble vs sure: accept-reject of a 50/50 gamble against a guaranteed amount; offers individually calibrated to each subject's indifference point; gain-only + mixed trials; points currency with performance bonus up to GBP 20
budget_reported: 120 modelled trials (64 mixed + 56 gain-only, calibrated phase 2; 90 training trials not modelled)
design_points_basis: Each modelled trial is a distinct individually calibrated offer; no repeats reported; calibration concentrates trials at the identification margin
estimation_regime: Hierarchical Bayesian (hBayesDM/Stan); occasions fit SEPARATELY with separate group-level priors (per-occasion partial pooling across subjects; authors chose this explicitly to avoid inflating reliability)
notes: Joint-across-occasions model gives 0.87 (0.77-0.94); authors warn joint estimation inflates point-estimate reliability. NOT independent per-subject fits - direction-level comparison with CPC18 split-half Spearman only, never numeric equivalence
Joint model 0.90 (0.83-0.95); inverse temperature ICC(A,1) 0.80 (0.64-0.89). Same estimation-regime caveat

task_format: Accept-reject of 50/50 mixed two-outcome gambles from gain-loss factorial grids (Tom et al. 2007 style); NOT calibrated per subject
n_subjects: simulation: 6586 parameter combos / 329300 simulated datasets; plus 4 real subjects from Walasek & Stewart 2015
budget_reported: 64-100 unique gambles per set (8x8 or 10x10 grid); Sim 2: 64 gambles repeated up to 60x (3840 trials)
design_points_basis: Unique gain-loss combinations in the grid; repeats help little for lambda (recovered-lambda IQR 0.21 at 1x64 to 0.07 at 10x64, authors still judge it poorly recovered)
construct: loss aversion (lambda = -phi_loss/phi_gain from per-subject logistic regression)
reliability_value: quote: extremely poor parameter recoverability; lambda cannot be reliably estimated even in impractically large experiments
estimation_regime: Independent per-subject logistic regression (probit gives same result)
notes: Mechanism: tradeoff between lambda and bias/other parameters - a format/parametrization problem, so trial count alone does not rescue lambda (their Sim 2). AUIC (proportion of gambles accepted) is nearly perfectly recovered - direct parallel to CPC18 loss_avoid_adj (measurable) vs b_loss (flatline). Individual-difference attenuation: true r=.65 recovered as median .10 (range -.73 to .77). Literature trial counts they tabulate: 36-512, most 64-256

task_format: Accept-reject / risky choice; CPT fit to random splits of the Gloeckner & Pachur (2012) dataset (Cognition 123:21-32; two occasions 1 week apart per its abstract; exact N and trials-per-occasion NOT independently verified)
budget_reported: random splits within large balanced choice sets
design_points_basis: No defensible single design-points number; excluded from figure placement
reliability_type: split-half rank generalization (histograms; no single r quoted)
reliability_value: quote: extremely unreliable; no relation between participants' rank lambda in the first and second sets of choices
notes: THE source of the phrase 'extremely unreliable' (the Decision paper says 'extremely poor parameter recoverability' - cite each phrase to its own paper). Key problem-mix quote: 'it is the change of choice set that roundly kills generalization' - direct external support for CPC18's Set-composition confound

citation: Pedroni, Frey, Bruhin, Dutilh, Hertwig & Rieskamp (2017) Nature Human Behaviour 1:803-809
task_format: Six elicitation methods, incentivized: BART (30 balloons), CCT (84 rounds x 32 cards), adaptive lotteries (75-100 pairs, mean 80.6), marbles task (trial count in SI, not verified), MPL (56 pairs in 6 price lists), Holt & Laury (10 choices)
design_points_basis: Unique choices per method; no reliability-per-method values so no curve placement
construct: risk preference (method-level scores; CPT alpha/eta/lambda for MPL/adaptive lotteries/CCT)
reliability_type: convergent validity (cross-method rank correlation); NO test-retest in this paper
reliability_value: median cross-method r=.11 (range .06-.34); CPT parameters cross-method r ~.01-.12; only 13% of subjects in the same risk category across all six methods
notes: Task-format confound anchor: 'properties of the choice architecture - here, the EMs - strongly affect how individuals make their choice'; preferences 'constructed when they are elicited'. Median lambda varies by method: 1.36 (MPL), 1.64 (adaptive lotteries), 0.43 (CCT). Note printed range '(0.12 < r < 0.01)' is a typographic error in the published PDF, intended ~.01-.12
